emails.subject: A short video for the Riverbend team
emails.body:
Hi Riverbend team,

I made a short video showing what your shelter, crisis line and VOCA and FVPSA reporting would look like in one place, with Riverbend's name on it.

[VIDEO]

Who on your team would be the right person to talk to about this?

scenes.topic: VOCA and FVPSA without the quarter-end scramble
scenes.vo: Priya, I put this short video together for you, about grant reporting at Riverbend Family Shelter.

scenes.headline: Two funders. One set of *numbers* rebuilt by hand.
lines: Services logged in one place, demographics in another
VOCA and FVPSA each want them their own way
scenes.vo: With VOCA and FVPSA both funding Riverbend, the same services get counted twice, by hand, in two different formats.
In NECX, every case is tagged to the grant that funds it, so services count toward the right grant from day one.
For VOCA, NECX builds the OVC PMT screen sheet from your logged services, and checks it against OVC's own rules before sign-off.
The FVPSA report fills in from the same records.
And Explain shows every record behind a number, and anything left out.

scenes.headline: Count it once. *Report* it everywhere.
items: Every case tagged to its grant
scenes.vo: Count each service once, check it before you certify, and explain every number.

scenes.question: Would it help to see last quarter's VOCA report built this way?
scenes.vo: Would it help to see last quarter's VOCA report built this way? Just reply to this email.

emails.subject: VOCA and FVPSA, counted once
emails.body:
Hi Priya,

With VOCA and FVPSA both funding Riverbend, I'm guessing the same services get counted twice each quarter, in two formats.

I recorded a one-minute video showing how NECX builds both reports from one set of case records.

[VIDEO]

Would it help to see last quarter's VOCA report built this way?
Hi Priya, making sure the video reached you. If reporting sits with someone else at Riverbend, a name is all I need.

emails.subject: The FVPSA numbers behind each line
emails.body:
Hi Priya,

One more thing that grants teams tell us matters at certification time: in NECX, every number in the FVPSA report opens to the records behind it, and shows anything left out and why.

That makes the questions from a program officer much faster to answer.

Is that something you deal with at Riverbend?

emails.subject: Closing the loop
emails.body:
Hi Priya,

I'll stop here so I'm not filling your inbox. If quarter-end reporting ever becomes a priority at Riverbend, just reply and I'll set up a short walkthrough with your own grants.

Thanks for the work your team does.

scenes.vo: Marcus, this is a short video I made for you, about running the shelter side of Riverbend.

scenes.headline: Tonight's *bed count* lives on a whiteboard.
lines: The waitlist is a separate spreadsheet
scenes.vo: When the bed count lives on a whiteboard and the waitlist in a spreadsheet, intake is always guessing.
Here's NECX with Riverbend's name on it. Beds, hotline and what needs attention, the moment you sign in.
Every bed is available, occupied, reserved, or out of service, so tonight's count is the real count.
The waitlist sits right beside your beds.
And when a family needs a partner shelter, you choose exactly what goes with the referral.

scenes.headline: One live view of the *whole* shelter.
scenes.vo: One live bed board, the waitlist beside it, and referrals that share only what you choose.

scenes.question: Worth a 20-minute look with your own room layout?
scenes.vo: Worth a twenty-minute look with your own room layout? Just reply to this email.

emails.subject: Every bed at Riverbend, live
emails.body:
Hi Marcus,

Running 40 beds and a crisis line means intake needs the real bed count, not last night's whiteboard.

I made you a one-minute video with Riverbend's name on a live bed board, the waitlist beside it, and referrals to partner shelters.

[VIDEO]

Worth a 20-minute look with your own room layout?
Hi Marcus, checking the video came through. If someone else runs intake at Riverbend, I'm happy to send it their way.

emails.subject: Last note from me
emails.body:
Hi Marcus,

I won't keep following up. If the bed board or the waitlist ever becomes a headache at Riverbend, reply here and I'll show you how other shelters run it.

Thank you for the work you do.

emails.subject: Who handles grant reporting?
emails.body:
Hi Dana,

I'm trying to reach whoever owns VOCA and FVPSA reporting at Riverbend. Could you point me to the right person?

Thank you.
